subject: Globex RFI: model provenance, license compatibility, and repinning procedure

Cc: procurement@globex.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 13:21:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: model catalog origins, licensing, and version pinning

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. Attached is the RFI we referenced; the security and procurement teams are particularly focused on three areas: 1) license compatibility across downstream redistribution/use (OSS + commercial mixes), 2) deterministic provenance records (origin of model weights, training data at a high level), and 3) a documented process for pinning and rolling back model versions in production.

Could you confirm whether Redwood can provide per-model license metadata and an auditable pinning workflow that we can map into our vendor controls? A few specific asks are in the attachment (Globex_RFI_ModelCatalog_20270415.pdf).

Thanks,
Tara Singh
Sr. Procurement Manager
Globex Corporation

Thanks for the RFI and the clear asks. I've looped in Marissa (Sales lead) and Neha (Product trust) to prepare a consolidated response. High-level: yes, Redwood maintains per-model license metadata, a model provenance record (hashes, source repo references, and a published manifest when available), and a documented pinning/rollback playbook we can share. We'll aim to send a detailed, itemized workbook back by Monday. If you have a preferred format (spreadsheet vs PDF), let us know — we usually return a matrix (catalog row per model) plus an appendixed playbook for pin/rollback.

Best,

Tara —

Attached is the workbook (Redwood_Response_ModelCatalog_20270419.xlsx) in draft form. Key highlights here:

- License metadata: each catalog entry includes a license field (SPDX where available), the maintainer/source, and a license-compatibility note we compile for common downstream uses (embedding redistribution, model rehosting, commercial redistribution). Nonstandard or dual licenses have commentary and a recommended enterprise-safe usage (for example, use-as-service only).

- Provenance: we publish a model manifest that includes the published artifact hash, origin tarball URL or commit id (for open-source models), and training data provenance summary (dataset names/curation notes where allowed). For closed-source vendor models we surface vendor-provided attestations and ingestion timestamps. All manifests are time-stamped and signed with an internal key for audit purposes.

- Pinning and rollbacks: our private and dedicated customers can pin model versions by model_id+artifact_hash; the platform supports automated canary rollouts and an immediate rollback API call that restores previous weights and KV cache compatibility rules. We include an ordered checklist for pre- and post-rollout QA in the attached playbook.

See the last tab of the workbook for the procedural checklist and a suggested SLA for advance notification on model deprecations.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Response_ModelCatalog_20270419.xlsx (spreadsheet, draft)

Marissa / Vivek —

Thanks for the workbook. A few legal clarifications before we can map this to our compliance matrix: 1) your "license-compatibility note" column — is it produced by automated parsing or legal review? Can you supply evidence for the determination (e.g., SPDX mapping, counsel memo)? 2) For models that allow "use-as-service" but disallow redistribution, how does Redwood enforce downstream restrictions when we rehost locally or provide fine-tuning to our teams? 3) For pinning and rollback, is the artifact hash anchored in a tamper-evident ledger or timestamping service that we can independently verify?

If you can provide short attestations per item and a copy of your internal manifest schema (redacted fields are fine), that would expedite vendor sign-off.

Regards,
Alex Hudson
Senior Counsel, Globex Corporation

Subject: Re: RFI: clarifications on license compatibility and derivative work definition

Alex / Tara —

Appreciate the careful questions. Quick answers and next steps below (we'll follow up with the redacted manifest and a short counsel note by EOD):

1) License-compatibility note: produced by a two-step process — automated SPDX-first pass that flags uncommon terms + a human review by our product trust team for edge cases. We attach the SPDX parsing output and a summary memo for any model where automated parsing disagrees with the product trust assessment.

2) Downstream enforcement: for hosted/Redwood-managed deployments we enforce usage constraints via contractual terms and API-level feature flags (limiting export of model weights, logging of fine-tuning artifacts). For dedicated/private deployments (where you control the environment) we provide recommended contractual language, a stewardship checklist, and optional policy agents (post-deployment compliance hooks) that Globex can run. We also document recommended operational controls (e.g., disable weight export, restrict shell access to inference nodes).

3) Artifact anchoring: model artifacts are hashed and timestamped. For enterprise customers we can produce signed manifests (signed by our KMS-managed key) and publish the manifest hash to a timestamping service (we support RFC-compliant timestamping with an external timestamp authority). That gives you an independently verifiable chain-of-custody.

Deliverables we'll provide by EOD: redacted manifest schema (JSON fields list), SPDX parsing outputs for the models you listed, and a short counsel-backed attestation template you can attach to your vendor file. I've cc'd Neha (product trust) — she will own the deliverables and can do a quick call if Alex wants to walk through the manifest fields.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
